title: 5-Fold Spatial Block Cross-Validation Enhanced MaxEnt Species Distribution Modeling with MESS Extrapolation Risk Assessment for Ophiocordyceps sinensis on the Tibetan Plateau
author: Qiuyang Wei

steps.title: Collect and filter occurrence data
steps.instruction: Gather Ophiocordyceps sinensis records from GBIF, Discover Life, ESPECIES platform, and published surveys; remove duplicate lat/lon entries, records outside the China boundary mask (GS (2022)1873), and any with coordinate uncertainty >10 km; visually inspect for geocoding errors; apply ENMTools v1.1.2 spatial thinning with a random algorithm and a 10 km minimum nearest‑neighbor distance, producing 201 spatially independent points saved as occurrences_filtered_201pts.csv (species, longitude, latitude). Document the number of records removed at each cleaning step.

steps.title: Prepare environmental predictor layers
steps.instruction: Download WorldClim v2.1 bioclimatic variables (bio_1–bio_19, 30‑arcsecond resolution) and HWSD v2.0 soil variables (16 pedological variables for 0–30 cm topsoil); derive slope and aspect from a DEM using ArcGIS Spatial Analyst (Surface > Slope/Aspect); obtain BCC‑CSM2‑MR SSP3‑7.0 climate projections for 2021–2040 and 2041–2060; reproject all layers to WGS84, resample to 30‑arcsecond (~1 km²) using bilinear interpolation, and clip to the China boundary mask; verify identical extent, resolution, and CRS; run an initial MaxEnt v3.4.1 model with all 38 variables, 10,000 background points, 500 iterations, logistic output, and exclude variables with percent contribution <0.1%; compute a Pearson correlation matrix across occurrence locations with ENMTools v1.1.2 and remove one variable from each pair with |r| ≥ 0.8, keeping the more ecologically relevant one, resulting in a final set of 16 predictors: alt, bio_1, bio_3, bio_4, bio_5, bio_17, bio_18, aspect, slope, t_caco3, t_esp, t_gravel, t_oc, t_ph_h2o, t_silt, t_usda_tex.

steps.title: Tune and run MaxEnt models
steps.instruction: Perform hyperparameter tuning by testing regularization multipliers 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 and feature‑class combinations L, LQ, LQH, LQHP, LQHPT with 5‑fold spatial block cross‑validation (SBCV); select the combination with the highest mean test AUC (optimal: feature classes = LQH, regularization multiplier = 1.0). Configure the final MaxEnt v3.4.1 run with 500 maximum iterations, 10,000 stratified random background points, logistic output, 11 bootstrap replicates per SBCV fold (total 55 runs), fixed random seed = 42, and jackknife analysis enabled. Evaluate performance using mean test AUC across all SBCV folds and bootstrap replicates (expected mean test AUC = 0.953 ± 0.002), mean training AUC = 0.963 ± 0.001, omission rate at FCV1 threshold, and TSS (expected ≈ 0.85; TSS = Sensitivity + Specificity − 1, values > 0.5 indicate reliability). Finally, train on all 201 occurrence points with the optimal hyperparameters and generate 11 bootstrap replicates, averaging them to produce the final suitability map.

steps.title: Compute MESS extrapolation risk
steps.instruction: Extract values of the 16 optimized predictors at all 201 occurrence points; split into training (n = 180, 90 %) and test (n = 21, 10 %) sets; standardize each variable to Z‑scores using training set mean and SD, applying the same parameters to the test set. In Python 3.9, calculate for each variable i and occurrence j the similarity index Si,j based on the training min‑max range using the piecewise formulas provided, weight each Si,j by the variable’s percent contribution from the MaxEnt model, and sum across all 16 predictors to obtain the total MESS score (range = −∞ to 1.0). Classify risk: Low (Si ≥ 0.8), Moderate (0.5 ≤ Si < 0.8), High (0.2 ≤ Si < 0.5), Very High (0 ≤ Si < 0.2), Extreme (Si < 0). Note that reported MESS values describe only the 201 occurrence localities (mean MESS = 0.734 ± 0.135; no extreme‑risk samples). Flag projected grid cells with low MESS scores for cautious interpretation.

steps.title: Classify habitat suitability and project temporally
steps.instruction: In ArcGIS 10.8, apply a primary suitability threshold of 0.70 (lower bound justified by a minimum occurrence probability of 0.30 from field validation) to the final logistic suitability map; additionally evaluate alternative thresholds: the MaxSS threshold (maximizing training sensitivity + specificity), the 10 % omission threshold (10 % of training localities omitted), and interval shifts of ±0.05 (0.25 and 0.35) around the lower bound. Compare area estimates and spatial patterns across thresholds. Project the final MaxEnt model onto (a) historical baseline climate (WorldClim 1970–2000), (b) near‑term climate (BCC‑CSM2‑MR SSP3‑7.0 2021–2040), and (c) mid‑century climate (BCC‑CSM2‑MR SSP3‑7.0 2041–2060), keeping soil and terrain layers constant. Using SDM Toolbox v2.5, quantify net habitat area change relative to the baseline suitable area of 396,000 km², identify expansion and contraction zones, calculate distribution centroid shifts (km and direction), and express all percentage changes with the baseline denominator.

steps.title: Statistical analysis and reporting
steps.instruction: Report mean ± SD of training and test AUC and TSS across all SBCV folds and bootstrap replicates; report omission rates at the FCV1 threshold (mean ± SD); present MaxEnt variable percent contribution and permutation importance; provide spatial block statistics (mean prediction probability and training‑test differences per block); summarize MESS statistics (mean ± SD, range, and proportion of occurrence points in each risk category); give habitat area estimates in km² and as a percentage of China’s land area, always stating the denominator (baseline 396,000 km²); and assess threshold sensitivity by reporting the range of area estimates across all tested thresholds.
